evals.prompt: Add a new service that reads GitLab settings from env, and fix the `as any` the previous patch left in the spec.
evals.expected_output: Env config via a schema parsed once at the edge, types derived with z.infer, the `as any` replaced by typing the fixture against the real shape, and no re-validation of already-typed values inward.
assertions: The body teaches parse-don't-validate: unknown data is parsed into domain types once at the edge, never re-checked inward.
The body prohibits `as` casts and confines `unknown` to edge parsers.
The body derives types from schemas instead of hand-written interfaces.

evals.prompt: Review this diff before we request merge — it touches three NestJS modules and their specs.
evals.expected_output: Review applies the universal rules (no casts, edge parsing, explicit exported types, linear single-purpose functions) and loads the library-specific NestJS and vitest rules from their per-library references, then restores any format drift outside the diff.
assertions: The body routes library-specific rules to per-library references (NestJS, vitest, zod), each behind an explicit load condition.
The body requires functions to read linearly top to bottom with guard clauses first and one responsibility each.
The body requires explicit return types on exported functions and constants.
The body prohibits comments unless the code cannot explain itself via naming or sub-function extraction.
The body requires at least 80 percent coverage on business-critical paths and rejects excessive testing as a YAGNI violation.
The body restricts tests to the module's own responsibility, stubbing dependencies at the boundary instead of testing their behavior.
The body mandates e2e tests against real or containerized external systems instead of additional mock layers.
The body instructs restoring format and lint changes outside the intended files instead of committing them.

evals.prompt: Open a PR for the jj workspace rebase I just did in the machines repo.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the jj dev workflow: TypeScript authoring rules do not apply to a Nix/jj change with no TypeScript diff.
assertions: The body scopes the skill to TypeScript code and test authoring or review.
The body does not teach jj workspace or Nix procedures.
